SUMMARY: hairstyle a long low rope braid with parted curtain bangs and its end curving forward over the shoulder; costume a long leather coat with a bandolier of glass vials, brass goggles and long gloves — a mysterious experimenter's shape; design idea Curved bands of overlapping leather converge into a silver capsule closure at the sternum, then fan back toward the coat side seams like a branching ray pattern.; face a stoic, unreadable reserve, light honey-beige skin, face with soft jaw angles that taper gently toward a rounded chin, not wide from the front; expression proud and poised.
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Californium (캘리포늄) itself — the sovereign of the Californium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: late twenties — a clear adult face with soft, smooth contours; no wrinkles, folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a stoic, unreadable reserve; light honey-beige skin; face with soft jaw angles that taper gently toward a rounded chin, not wide from the front; phoenix eyes with gracefully lifted outer corners, of natural size; steel-blue eyes; thin straight brows; petite straight nose; soft medium lips.
Body and hair: curvy build; a long low rope braid with parted curtain bangs and its end curving forward over the shoulder; deep honey-gold hair streaked with brilliant sun-white strands, as if bleached by a coastal sun.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: a proud, poised look with a faint closed-lip smile.
Her element, carried in her design: californium: a silvery synthetic metal first made in 1950 by striking curium with alpha particles, and named for the golden western land and university where she was born, a land itself named after a legendary island of gold at the western edge of the world, ruled by a queen of warrior women armed in gold; one of her forms splits apart on its own, so a single microgram pours out over two million neutrons every second, an invisible spray used to kindle new nuclear reactors, to find hidden veins of gold and silver and pockets of oil deep underground, to spot concealed explosives and to fight cancer, and a single gram of her is worth tens of millions.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a long leather coat with a bandolier of glass vials, brass goggles and long gloves — a mysterious experimenter's shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Design idea: Curved bands of overlapping leather converge into a silver capsule closure at the sternum, then fan back toward the coat side seams like a branching ray pattern.
Colours: sun-streaked honey gold, blazing sunset coral, sun-baked bronze, clear ocean turquoise.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1910, the first great flying meet on a sun-baked coastal plain: biplanes and a small dirigible soaring over golden hills, grandstands under striped awnings, and wooden oil derricks lined up along the horizon.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Stance and hands: Her wrists fall outside the coat edges and both empty hands are unobstructed.
Setting detail: Sunlit judging pavilion with copper railings, clear sky and a small dirigible far over the field.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Cf) and atomic number (98) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
